why: The statement asks only for infinitude for every non-square a other than -1, unconditionally. So every GRH-conditional or hypothesis-conditional result (Hooley, Perucca-Shparlinski, Kimmel, Fan-Pollack, Goldmakher-Martin-Péringuey, Cherubini-Perucca, the Järviniemi papers, Murty-Naik) is a different-hypothesis variant. Gupta-Murty and Heath-Brown prove infinitude for an unspecified member of a finite set, which settles no given a, and KST is an almost-all average; I scored these as variants rather than cases, since none fixes any a. The OpenAI family-029 main claim, an unconditional c_a·x/(log x)^2 lower bound, answers the whole question as worded, and the missing density is not asked for. It is unreviewed. I rated it doubtful rather than not_credible: the analytic input is extraordinary, but no specific error has been identified and the release is a serious, documented one. openai-029-main-2026 and openai-math-029 are the same manuscript (the second was read from source and also bundles the simultaneous companion). I answered both identically. AI role is generated: the release-level README sentence credits the model, and 029 is not among the named exceptions. The Lean formalisation is scope none (formalising a claimed proof), with coding assistants only. Carella 2017 predates the snapshot and is not_credible, given nine years of silence, retitling after a long dormancy, and the concrete gaps the record lists.
doubts: openai-029-main-2026 and openai-math-029 duplicate one manuscript (dates 4 Oct folder name vs 6 Oct public). The AI attribution for 029 rests on a release-level sentence, not on a 029-specific acknowledgement. Calling Gupta-Murty, Heath-Brown and KST variant rather than case was a close call; it does not change the outcome, because both pre-date the snapshot or are dominated by the whole claim.
